title: Per-token delta pricing pilot + enterprise commit floor with security questionnaire gating
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Run a controlled pilot to test a per-token "delta" pricing model that explicitly separates ingress (input) and egress (output/streaming) unit rates, paired with an enterprise committed minimum (monthly floor) option. We will measure revenue impact, customer acceptance, contract conversion, and operational complexity. 

Background: Customers increasingly ask for asymmetric pricing (lower input rates for heavy embedding/prompt workloads, higher output rates for long generations/streaming). Prior internal proposals explored asymmetric token ladders and crediting; this pilot focuses on: 1) explicit per-token delta (IngressRate != EgressRate), 2) a streaming per-second/stream-token surcharge option, and 3) an enterprise monthly commit floor that smooths revenue and simplifies contract negotiations. This ticket coordinates PM, Billing, Legal (contract language), and Security (SQ answers) to ensure we can present the model in RFP/SQ responses.

Experiment design: 
- Variants: Control (current symmetric rate), Variant A (Ingress = $0.0008/1k, Egress = $0.0024/1k), Variant B (Ingress = $0.0005/1k, Egress = $0.0030/1k + streaming surcharge $0.10/min equivalent), Variant C (same as B + enterprise monthly floor option: $10k/month minimum with discounted per-token rates).
- Cohorts: New signups (opt-in A/B), existing enterprise prospects (sales-driven offer for Variant C), and a holdout group.
- Duration: 8 weeks with interim check at week 3 for business-safety signals.
- Primary metrics: revenue per active customer, conversion rate from trial to commit, average invoice delta, churn lift, and complaints/tickets. Secondary metrics: average request latency, # of billing disputes, console UX errors.

Implementation notes: 
- Billing: Billing team to implement per-token ingress/egress counters; streaming surcharge is additive and reported separately on invoices. Metering should be feature-flagged per account (flag: pricing.delta_io_experiment).
- API/Docs: SDK and API docs must clearly show Ingress vs Egress units and streaming surcharges. Console should display a sample monthly estimate under the selected pricing variant.
- Contracting & SQ: Legal to prepare a standard enterprise-floor addendum + template language for security questionnaire responses that reference meter collection, retention of logs, encryption at rest/in transit, and limited disclosure of billing telemetry. Security to pre-approve SQ language for customers asking about auditability and data residency.

Rollout & gating: 
- Soft launch to 10% of new free-tier signups and 3 strategic enterprise pilots (sales-nominated).
- Safety checks: If disputes > 0.5% of billings in any cohort over a week OR NPS drop > 4 pts in cohorts, pause.

Success criteria (to declare experiment positive): 
- Variant C (enterprise floor option) results in >= 20% higher MRR for participating contracts after 3 months vs historical cohorts, and minimal increase in billing disputes (<0.2% absolute). 
- Variant A or B increases revenue per active user by >= 8% without significant negative UX feedback.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Customer confusion: invest in clear billing visualizations and sample invoices. 
- Legal/SQ friction slowing sales: prepare pre-approved SQ language and a short FAQ for procurement. 
- Technical debt in billing pipeline: flag rollouts and include a rollback plan, meter-level reconciliation job scheduled daily.

Next steps: 
1) Review pricing numbers with Finance (done 2025-02-12, see attachment). 
2) Billing and Engineering to estimate implementation effort (ENG ticket dependency below). 
3) Draft enterprise-floor addendum and SQ language with Legal & Security. 
4) Wire up dashboard cards and sample invoices in Console for early QA.
